=== DEFAULT KNOWLEDGE (always-true facts about this environment) ===
The available actions are: up, down, left, right, noop, and click ROW COL, where ROW is the row index and COL is the column index (both 0-indexed; this matches the (row, col) order the perception reports cells in).
=== END DEFAULT KNOWLEDGE ===

=== WORLD KNOWLEDGE (general facts; may be empty) ===
- The grid is 20 rows (0–19) and 20 columns (0–19), background black.
- Three colored objects exist: green, red, yellow.
- Green: three vertical cells at rows 17, 18, 19 with the same column. Every step, their column decreases by 1 (wrapping from 0 to 19); rows never change.
- Yellow: a single cell. Every step, its column decreases by 1 (wrapping from 0 to 19); its row never changes.
- Red: a fixed shape of six cells (relative positions preserved). Its movement depends only on the action:
  - On `noop`: if the maximum row among red cells is 19, then red does not move; otherwise every red cell’s row increases by 1 (downward).
  - On `up`: every red cell’s row decreases by 6 (upward).
  - If a red cell’s row would fall outside [0,19] after a move, that cell disappears and is never seen again.
- When red is absent, the actions `noop` and `up` produce the same observable change (only green and yellow shift left), so they cannot be distinguished from state features alone.
- Actions `down`, `left`, `right`, and `click` are not observed in the provided examples; their effects are unknown.
- The background and all other cells remain unchanged.
=== END WORLD KNOWLEDGE ===

Below is a trajectory of consecutive states (summarized as features by a perception module) with the action taken between each pair. ONE action is hidden and marked `??? (IDENTIFY THIS)`. Use the WHOLE trajectory -- the states and actions BEFORE and AFTER the gap -- to infer the hidden action; temporally-extended patterns (a selected/active object, momentum, periodicity) may only be visible across several steps.

record.inv_response:
<reasoning>Between state t‑1 and state t the green cells move left one column as usual.  
The red cells are unchanged from state t‑1 to state t.  
A `noop` action leaves the red shape unchanged when its maximum row is 19 (which it is: rows 16–19).  
An `up` action would shift every red cell upward by 6 rows, changing their positions.  
Since the red cells stay the same, the hidden action cannot be `up`; it must be `noop`.</reasoning>
<actions>
noop
</actions>

classification: Secondary semantic match; belief states equivalent floor condition but does not name the learned flag.
findings: P19 adds active per-color boundary predicates, including red:bottom.
B20 (child19) changes noop from unconditional fall to staying when maximum red row is19, the same geometric condition.
B20 and cached traces describe retained coordinates rather than explicitly consuming red:bottom; this is weaker coupling than Magnets/SET/Disease.
Frames100-103 show fall, landing, staying at floor, then a six-row net jump; the jump was already predicted correctly before B20.
Separate floor-contact cached records show improvements; do not attribute those cache results to uncached steps100/101.
B20 is an explored branch; saved best18 is a different lineage.
